notes:
- Customer: mid-size e-discovery / compliance platform used by corporate legal teams and law firms.
- Primary pain: current vector search (open-source) has unpredictable tail latency for long docs and rerank costs explode at scale. Wants per-query cost predictability.
- Quote from CTO: "We need a deterministic cost model for discovery queries; spikes in rerank time kill margins."
- Index scale: estimate 20M-30M documents, average doc length ~6k tokens, expecting heavy prefix reuse across queries.
- Latency target: 200-350ms for top-K retrieval + rerank under typical query traffic (~120 QPS sustained) with ability to burst to 500 QPS for e-discovery collection windows.
- Cost sensitivity: target below $0.10/query (all-in) for steady-state; willing to trade slight latency for lower unit cost.
- Model preferences: open LLaMA-family variants for rerank; embedding model must be deterministic & localizable (customer won't allow any third-party endpoint).
- Routing/fallback: wants automatic fallback to smaller quantized model variant if dedicated capacity is throttled; strict audit trail required for all fallback events.
- Retention & audit: 7+ year legal retention for evidence with item-level audit logs; immutability window request for POC.
- Integration notes: currently uses S3-like object store in customer VPC; expects Redwood Private to run in customer's cloud account or on-prem appliance.
- POC success metrics: 1) 95th percentile retrieval+rerank latency <= 350ms; 2) average cost/query <= $0.10; 3) audit log proof-of-concept with searchable events.
- Informal: AE notes that procurement cycles are long; prioritize security deliverables to unblock.
